nodes.label: [Requirement] Assignment Required Outputs
nodes.rationale: Assignment-required delivery files: train.py for PPO training with checkpoints and TensorBoard; test.py for repeatable RL-vs-baseline evaluation writing CSV; play.py for human graphical mode; observe.py for episode visualization; evaluate.ipynb for plots/tables; README.md for install/run instructions; pyproject.toml plus uv.lock for the uv project; PDF slides/report covering game, MDP, PPO rationale, custom architecture, hyperparameters, baseline, implementation, results, references and original contribution; deadline 31/12/2026.
nodes.source_location: Word document text/tables; §7.1 lines 150-160; Appendix A lines 239-240

nodes.label: [Proposed] Attack Normalized Observation
nodes.rationale: Tactical geometry and match context normalized by pitch scale and attack direction; facing represented as sin(theta), cos(theta); score difference clipped to a reasonable range; observation must be tested for finite values, stable ordering and identical semantics for both attack directions.

nodes.label: [Proposed] Original Continuous Five Action Proposal
nodes.rationale: Original historical proposal: five continuous values horizontal move [-1,1], vertical move [-1,1], effort [0,1], kick trigger [0,1], kick power [0,1]; kick trigger and power are separate and there is no separate kick-direction action; retained as the historical plan proposal while the current implemented engine uses the later discrete nine-direction hybrid action, so the original proposal is not silently rewritten.

nodes.label: [Requirement] Customized MLP Architecture Not Implemented
nodes.rationale: The implementation must use a genuinely customized neural-network architecture, as required by the project brief; the customized MLP requirement is not implemented yet while the PPO baseline training itself is still planned.

nodes.label: [Planned] Evaluation Protocol
nodes.rationale: Metrics: win/draw/loss rate, goal difference and goals for/against, shots and goals per shot, controlled-possession share, turnovers by cause, ball recoveries separating steals from loose-ball recoveries, attacking progress and time in attacking half, stamina profile, sanity and exploit diagnostics; reproducible evaluation with held-out seeds, swapping attack direction and matching conditions for RL and baseline; save per-match results to CSV and show plots/tables in evaluate.ipynb.

nodes.label: [Original plan] Executive Summary
nodes.rationale: Consolidates the assignment brief: modern 2D top-down 1v1 football, autonomous agent against a transparent rule-based baseline, graphical and headless modes, PPO as first/baseline DRL algorithm, customized neural-network requirement, undiscounted reward logging, multi-metric comparison, CSV/plots/notebook, PDF report; deadline 31 December 2026 and team size 4; planning note marks reward values and low-level physics constants as experimental starting points, not guaranteed optimal settings.

nodes.label: [Planned] Feature Freeze Nineteen December
nodes.rationale: Freeze new features by 19 December and reserve 20-30 December for stabilization and submission; no new features after 19 December unless they fix a blocker or correctness bug.

nodes.label: [Original plan] Free Ball Physics
nodes.rationale: Free-ball physics: kick releases the ball with power-dependent initial velocity and friction; approved starting tuning constant deceleration 100 units/s^2 with reference speed 300 units/s stopping after 3 seconds and travelling 450 units; weaker rolls stop sooner; reference speed does not finalize maximum kick speed mapping.

nodes.label: [Proposed] Goal Opening One Hundred Twenty Units
nodes.norm_label: [proposed] goal opening one hundred twenty units
nodes.rationale: Goal rule: ball must fully cross the goal line inside the goal opening to score; opening about 120 units wide, centered on short boundaries.

nodes.label: [Original plan] Goal Restart Phase
nodes.rationale: Goal restart: register the goal exactly once, then enter a controlled restart phase; scoring does not automatically terminate the match.

nodes.label: [Planned] Interface Handoffs
nodes.rationale: Shared responsibilities and handoffs: every phase all four review a short demo and update issues or tasks; weekly integration checkpoint merging working code to main only after smoke test; Member A and C agree on state names and event timing before implementation; Member C and D agree on observation and action tensor shapes before PPO training; Member A and B verify graphical and headless modes use the same simulation; Member B and C verify rule-based opponent and RL agent receive equivalent mechanics; Member D coordinates final documentation.

nodes.label: [Tentative] Hardware Training Target
nodes.rationale: Initial hardware target: RTX 3060 6 GB VRAM; environment may be CPU-bound; benchmark actual environment steps per second and GPU memory before choosing total training timesteps; target not verified.

nodes.label: [Planned] Held Out Seeds
nodes.rationale: Aim for about 100 evaluation matches per comparison if runtime allows; if fewer are possible, report the exact sample size and uncertainty rather than overstating results; use held-out seeds and evaluate both attacking sides.

nodes.label: [Original plan] Hybrid Ball Model
nodes.rationale: Hybrid ball model: in controlled possession the ball follows a small offset in front of the carrier; on kick it becomes free with power-dependent initial velocity and friction; either player may recover a free ball.

nodes.label: [Original plan] Low Stamina Speed Reduction
nodes.rationale: Low stamina reduces speed and acceleration with linear speed/acceleration factors down to 50 percent at empty; stamina beginning settings are experimental starting values, not frozen optimal tuning.

nodes.label: [Original plan] Match Duration Sixty Seconds
nodes.rationale: Match length: 60 seconds of simulated time; higher score wins; ties are draws; clock policy explicitly tested around restarts.

nodes.label: [Original plan] One Shot Goal Event
nodes.rationale: A confirmed goal is registered exactly once and then the restart phase begins; goals do not automatically end the match.

nodes.label: [Original plan] Out Of Bounds Last Touch
nodes.norm_label: [original plan] out of bounds last touch
nodes.rationale: Out of bounds: the last player to touch is responsible, loses the ball, and the opponent restarts from the exit location; responsible player resets near their own goal; receiver starting in controlled possession is a proposed default to confirm.

nodes.label: [Planned] Phase One Design
nodes.rationale: Phase P1 Design and interfaces from 24-30 Oct: confirm mechanics, define state/action/observation/reward interfaces, set repository layout, establish coding conventions and tests; short design spec agreed, action and observation shapes fixed, each module has an owner.

nodes.label: [Planned] Phase Eight Integration
nodes.rationale: Phase P8 Integration and submission from 14-30 Dec: bug fixes, reproduce clean setup via uv sync, README, PDF slides, demo recording or live demo, final repo audit; all required files run from README and clean install verified.

nodes.label: [Original plan] Physics Update Sixty Hertz
nodes.rationale: Physics simulation at 60 Hz with fixed dt = 1/60 second; one physics update is 1/60 second; a 60 second match contains 3,600 physics updates.

nodes.label: [Proposed] Pitch Proposal Eight Hundred By Five Hundred
nodes.norm_label: [proposed] pitch proposal eight hundred by five hundred
nodes.rationale: Logical pitch proposal of 800 x 500 units (8:5); centered goal openings about 120 units wide on left/right short boundaries; player radius 15; players near (200,250) and (600,250); ball at (400,250); dimensions and markings are initial implementation values to validate, not requirements imposed by the assignment.

nodes.label: [Original plan] Policy Decision Ten Hertz
nodes.rationale: Policy decides at 10 Hz, one decision every 6 physics updates; the action is held for six physics updates; a 60 second match contains approximately 600 policy decisions.

nodes.label: [Tentative] Potential Shaping Lambda Two
nodes.rationale: Attacking ball progress uses potential-based shaping with lambda initially 2 as an experiment; use attack-normalized ball-position potential in [0,1] and compare potential before and after transitions; this is a test value, not a guarantee against reward hacking.

nodes.label: [Original plan] PPO Baseline Algorithm
nodes.rationale: PPO (Proximal Policy Optimization) is the first/baseline DRL algorithm because the planned action space is continuous; PPO is the baseline algorithm, not a claim that PPO will be the best final algorithm.

nodes.label: [Proposed] PPO Observation Candidate
nodes.rationale: Recommended PPO observation: flat vector of normalized numeric features, mostly player-relative and attack-normalized; reduces left/right side bias and avoids image-based learning; final observation features are not yet finalized.

nodes.label: [Original plan] Reward Hacking Checks
nodes.rationale: Reward-hacking checks: deliberately lose and recover the ball repeatedly; shuttle the ball back and forth; kick unnecessarily to farm progress; stall while preserving possession; force out-of-bounds loops; trigger the same event on consecutive frames; potential-based shaping must be consistent across transitions and never reset to grant free reward.

nodes.label: [Tentative] Reward Weights Experiment Zero
nodes.rationale: Tentative experiment-0 reward weights, not settled: score a goal +10, concede -10, win +5, draw 0, lose -5, steal from opponent +1, recover loose ball +0.5, maintain possession 0 initially, ball progress potential-based shaping lambda initially 2; values must be tested, logged separately and adjusted only with evidence.

nodes.label: [Original plan] Risks And Decisions To Validate Early
nodes.norm_label: [original plan] risks and decisions to validate early
nodes.rationale: Risks and decisions to validate early: physics differs between modes; ball tunnelling or missed goal; reward hacking; sparse or unstable learning; overfitting to one side or seed; slow training; late integration; unclear restart semantics; mitigations include single simulation core, substep or swept collision checks, event-once guards, cautious reward shaping, direction randomization, early throughput benchmark and explicit restart phase.

nodes.label: [Planned] Rule Based Opponent
nodes.rationale: Rule-based baseline first; self-play or RL opponents are optional extensions, not required for the baseline; baseline uses the same physics and stamina rules as the RL agent and documents deterministic rules and thresholds.

nodes.label: [Planned] Stable-Baselines3 Action Encoding
nodes.rationale: Continuous policy for movement/effort/power with kick trigger handled consistently with the chosen action parameterization; SB3 does not directly support a generic structured mixed action, so an explicit action encoding or custom distribution is required; C and D must agree before building the RL interface.

nodes.label: [Original plan] Shared Simulation Core
nodes.rationale: Shared game simulation layer must not depend on Pygame or rendering; headless training advances simulated time as fast as compute allows while graphical mode is paced for human play; both modes use the same simulation core.

nodes.label: [Proposed] Player Spawn Positions
nodes.rationale: Initial spawn positions: player A (200,250), player B (600,250), ball (400,250); randomize small starting variations only after deterministic reset works.

nodes.label: [Original plan] Stamina Reserve System
nodes.rationale: Stamina: each player starts at 100/100; sprint/high effort consumes stamina; low effort/rest recovers it; low stamina reduces speed and acceleration; initially no direct effect on kick accuracy, turning rate or tackling; kicking itself costs no stamina.

nodes.label: [Original plan] Steal Contact Contest
nodes.rationale: Steal/contact contest: a defender must remain close for a short interval before taking possession; cooldown prevents immediate possession toggling; exact thresholds and timings remain to be tuned.

nodes.label: [Original plan] Four Human Team Roles
nodes.rationale: Four-person work plan: Member A game engine and physics lead owning shared simulation core; Member B Pygame and gameplay baseline lead owning visual mode, human controls and rule-based opponent; Member C RL environment and reward lead owning Gymnasium wrapper, observation and reward events; Member D PPO, evaluation and release lead owning training, custom MLP, metrics and packaging.

nodes.label: [Planned] Training Diagnostics
nodes.rationale: Learning diagnostics: raw total episode reward undiscounted, moving average, reward-component breakdown, episode duration and end reason; PPO optimization diagnostics (policy loss, value loss, entropy, approximate KL, clip fraction, explained variance) that diagnose optimization but do not prove game skill; performance diagnostics (environment steps per second, elapsed wall time, CPU use, GPU memory).

nodes.label: [Requirement] Undiscounted Reward Logging
nodes.rationale: Assignment requirement: TensorBoard logging of total undiscounted reward per episode, with moving average if noisy; also log reward components and episode end reason.

nodes.label: [Implemented] Acceleration-based nine-direction movement
nodes.rationale: Eight directions plus idle, continuous effort, target-velocity acceleration, smooth turning, deceleration and persistent facing when stopped. Both players use identical equations; direction vectors are normalized except idle (0,0).

nodes.label: [Approved starting] Match clock runs through restarts
nodes.norm_label: [approved starting] match clock runs through restarts
nodes.rationale: Restart ticks count toward the 3,600-tick match clock and the match can finish during a restart; whether policies are queried during restarts is still an interface decision. Restart scaffolds currently freeze players, stamina and ball while the clock runs.

nodes.label: [Implemented] Locked engine dependency group
nodes.rationale: Engine tools (pytest, Ruff and locked transitive dependencies) live in the optional 'engine' group in pyproject.toml and uv.lock. Install with uv sync --locked --only-group engine to avoid pulling graphics/ML packages.

nodes.label: [Planned] Evaluation metrics and instrumentation
nodes.rationale: Metrics include win/draw/loss, goal difference, goals, shots/conversion, controlled possession, turnovers by cause, steals vs loose-ball recoveries, progress, stamina use, kick/idle frequency, out-of-bounds loops and throughput. Member A must supply reliable event identifiers, time, positions, transitions, scores, stamina and termination reasons.

nodes.label: [Planned] Facing-based kick with power mapping
nodes.rationale: Kick direction follows the player's facing; there is no independent aim direction. Trigger and power are chosen in the same decision step, with no charging mechanic. Not implemented: MovementAction currently rejects/ignores nothing but only models direction+effort.

nodes.label: [Implemented] 60 Hz physics and 10 Hz held decisions
nodes.norm_label: [implemented] 60 hz physics and 10 hz held decisions
nodes.rationale: Fixed dt = 1/60 s; one policy decision every 6 physics updates, holding the last action in between. Simulated time, not wall-clock time, determines match duration; step_decision stops early at the final whistle.

nodes.label: [Approved starting] Free-ball 300 units/s, 100 units/s², 3 s / 450 units
nodes.norm_label: [approved starting] free-ball 300 units/s, 100 units/s2, 3 s / 450 units
nodes.rationale: Approved constant deceleration 100 units/s² with a 300 units/s reference roll that stops in 3 s after 450 units; weaker rolls stop sooner. Reference speed is not a maximum kick speed or power mapping, and the ball is not pitch-clamped.
nodes.source_location: §3 'Ball, possession and stealing', line 73; docs/engine.md lines 117-133

nodes.label: [Implemented] full_stack test excluded from engine runs
nodes.norm_label: [implemented] full_stack test excluded from engine runs
nodes.rationale: The full_stack dependency-import smoke test needs the full project install and is intentionally excluded from engine-only runs, which use pytest -m 'not full_stack'. This means engine-only test success does not prove full-stack integration.

nodes.label: [Proposed] Full-ball goal crossing and restart
nodes.rationale: A goal occurs only when the ball fully crosses the goal line inside the opening; the event must register once, then enter a controlled restart. Scoring does not automatically terminate the match. No goal/score code exists yet.

nodes.label: [Planned] Headless and graphical modes
nodes.rationale: Headless mode enables fast training/testing; graphical mode is for interactive human play. Only headless inspection commands exist so far.

nodes.label: [Approved starting] Hybrid action: 9-direction + effort + binary kick + power
nodes.norm_label: [approved starting] hybrid action: 9-direction + effort + binary kick + power
nodes.rationale: direction is discrete with 9 choices (engine IDs 0-8: idle, N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW); effort and kick_power are continuous [0,1]; kick_trigger is binary and at most one request is consumed per decision. At least a binary kick trigger and once-per-decision consumption are approved; effort/power must not be silently discretized.

nodes.label: [Proposed] Hybrid controlled/free ball model
nodes.rationale: In controlled possession the ball follows a small offset in front of the carrier; on kick it becomes free with power-dependent initial velocity and friction; either player may recover a free ball. Only free-ball physics exists so far.

nodes.label: [Approved starting] Idle braking 40 units/s²
nodes.rationale: Constant idle braking clamped at zero to prevent reversal, preserving facing while coasting. At base speed 160 it takes 4 s to stop; this is the student's provisional choice and still needs play validation.
nodes.source_location: §3 'Player movement and stamina', line 66; docs/engine.md lines 46-47

nodes.label: [Implemented] 5 Nov engine foundation
nodes.rationale: Immutable snapshots, normalized directions, target-velocity acceleration, constant idle braking, smooth facing, pitch bounds, side-swapping reset, one-tick/six-tick stepping, a 60 s running clock, a one-shot terminal event, stamina, and free-ball motion exist. Kicks, possession, goals, collisions, RL wrapper and rendering do not; A phases are not all complete.
nodes.source_location: §16 'Implemented foundation and reproducible engine workflow', lines 283-289

nodes.label: [Open] Kick request timing, expiry and cooldown
nodes.norm_label: [open] kick request timing, expiry and cooldown
nodes.rationale: Exact kick-attempt timing, failed-request handling, phase-change handling and cooldown duration are unresolved. A first-tick attempt discarded on failure is a proposal, not approved; each new decision may issue a new request subject to possession/cooldown guards.

nodes.label: [Implemented] 60-second match clock (3,600 ticks)
nodes.rationale: 60 s of simulated time at 60 Hz, i.e. 3,600 physics ticks and 600 six-tick decision intervals. Remaining time derives from the integer tick; match_finished fires once at tick 3,600 and finished states never advance. Higher score wins, ties are draws.

nodes.label: [Proposed] Flat normalized observation vector
nodes.rationale: Candidate flat, player-relative and attack-normalized features: self position/velocity/facing/stamina, opponent relative state, ball relative state and possession category, tactical distances, remaining time and score difference. Final features are not confirmed; last toucher, reward components and prior progress should not be exposed automatically.

nodes.label: [Implemented] One-shot terminal event (goal/boundary events not implemented)
nodes.norm_label: [implemented] one-shot terminal event (goal/boundary events not implemented)
nodes.rationale: match_finished is emitted exactly once at tick 3,600 and finished states never advance again. The exactly-once rule is likewise required for goals, boundary crossings, steals and recoveries, and restart phases must prevent duplicate transitions; those events do not exist yet.

nodes.label: [Proposed] Out-of-bounds last-touch responsibility
nodes.rationale: The last player to touch is responsible, loses the ball, and the opponent restarts from the exit location while the responsible player resets near their own goal. Starting the receiver in controlled possession is only a proposed default.

nodes.label: [Planned] Member A phases A0-A7
nodes.rationale: A0 foundation, A1 player physics, A2 stamina, A3 ball dynamics, A4 contact/possession, A5 match rules, A6 integration, A7 hardening. Only A1, A2 and the first A3 increment are reported as implemented.

nodes.label: [Proposed] Pitch 800x500 with 120-unit goals
nodes.rationale: 800 x 500 logical units, centered 120-unit goal openings on left/right short boundaries, player radius 15. Implementation defaults to validate, not hard course requirements.

nodes.label: [Planned] PPO baseline with customized network
nodes.rationale: PPO is the chosen initial/baseline DRL algorithm and a customized neural-network architecture is required even when using Stable-Baselines3. Network architecture and hyperparameters remain open.

nodes.label: [Implemented] Python 3.12.14 pin
nodes.rationale: Interpreter version is pinned in .python-version (3.12.14); interpreters and dependencies must be recorded, never installed globally by hand.

nodes.label: [Implemented] Restart freeze/countdown scaffold
nodes.rationale: goal_restart and out_of_bounds_restart phases exist as testable scaffolding but no rule creates them. They freeze both player snapshots and the ball, decrement an integer countdown while the clock runs, and freeze stamina too. Actual placement, ownership, stamina recovery and policy querying remain undecided.

nodes.label: [Open] Reward exploit/anti-farming guards
nodes.rationale: The agent must not farm rewards by deliberately losing/recovering possession, kicking needlessly, moving back and forth, stalling or forcing boundaries. How to enforce this without double-counting or punishing legitimate kicks is not finalized.

nodes.label: [Proposed] Tentative reward weights
nodes.rationale: Experimental starting values only: goal +10, concede -10, win +5, draw 0, loss -5, steal +1, loose-ball recovery +0.5, possession duration 0 initially, potential-based progress shaping with lambda about 2, turnover/boundary penalty not finalized. Controlled possession means attached ball.

nodes.label: [Planned] Rule-based baseline comparison
nodes.rationale: A documented rule-based opponent and a justified multi-metric comparison against the RL agent are required; no baseline behaviour is implemented yet.

nodes.label: [Open] Stable-Baselines3 hybrid action encoding
nodes.rationale: A generic structured mixed action is not directly supported by Stable-Baselines3 PPO, so an explicit encoding or custom distribution is required. C/D must agree before building the RL interface.

nodes.label: [Planned] Single deterministic shared simulation core
nodes.rationale: One core must serve both headless RL training and graphical Pygame play so behaviour is identical in both modes; the renderer reads state but never owns physics.

nodes.label: [Implemented] Side-swapping reset
nodes.rationale: reset(swap_sides=True) swaps spawn positions, facing and attack orientations. The design intent is to evaluate both attacking directions and avoid left/right overfitting.

nodes.label: [Proposed] Single authoritative possession owner and last toucher
nodes.norm_label: [proposed] single authoritative possession owner and last toucher
nodes.rationale: Exactly one owner (A, B or none) is the single source of truth; per-player has_ball is derived. Last toucher is tracked separately. A ball cannot be both controlled and independently free in the same state.

nodes.label: [Proposed] Spawn positions A(200,250) B(600,250) ball(400,250)
nodes.rationale: Proposed initial spawns, now used by the implemented reset() for players and the stationary free ball at centre. Still tunable.

nodes.label: [Approved starting] Speed 160, acceleration 320, turn 2π/s
nodes.rationale: 5 Nov implementation defaults: max speed 160 units/s (800 units in 5 s), acceleration limit 320 units/s² (0 to full in 0.5 s / 30 ticks), turn rate 2π radians/s. Configurable starting values delegated by the student, not frozen tuning.
nodes.source_location: §3 'Player movement and stamina', line 68; docs/engine.md lines 35-44

nodes.label: [Implemented] Stamina consumption, recovery and fatigue
nodes.rationale: Implemented in game/stamina.py and integrated via step_player/simulation. Stamina updates first each tick; limits derive from base config; current velocity is never multiplied by fatigue. Requested non-idle effort costs energy even against a wall, and idle counts as rest. No kick cost.

nodes.label: [Approved starting] Stamina settings (100, 5/s, 100/15, neutral 0.5, 50% floor)
nodes.rationale: Max 100; full-effort drain 5 points/s (20 s to empty); idle recovery 100/15 points/s (15 s to full); neutral active effort 0.5; linear speed/acceleration factors down to 50% at empty. Approved experiment-0 values, not frozen optimal tuning.

nodes.label: [Proposed] Authoritative state schema and derived fields
nodes.norm_label: [proposed] authoritative state schema and derived fields
nodes.rationale: Persist player position/velocity/facing/stamina/contact timers, ball position/velocity/owner/last toucher, and match score/orientation/tick/phase/restart data. Derive remaining time, has_ball, dribble offset and geometry instead of duplicating them; avoid persistent Boolean flags that duplicate events.

nodes.label: [Proposed] Steal contest with cooldown
nodes.rationale: A defender must remain close for a short interval before taking possession; a cooldown prevents immediate possession toggling. Exact thresholds and timings remain to be tuned and no contest code exists yet.

nodes.label: [Documented] Five-continuous-value action superseded
nodes.rationale: The earlier Word-plan proposal of five continuous action values is superseded by the approved hybrid action. The graph must keep this historical difference instead of merging the two designs.

nodes.label: [Documented] Four-member team ownership
nodes.rationale: A owns engine/physics; B owns Pygame and the rule-based agent; C owns the Gymnasium wrapper, observations and rewards; D owns PPO, evaluation and delivery. Interfaces must be agreed before coding and modules are not silently changed.

nodes.label: [Planned] TensorBoard undiscounted episode return
nodes.rationale: Course deliverable requires total undiscounted reward per episode, with a moving average if noisy. Member D owns logging, but correct events start in the engine.

nodes.label: [Proposed] Provisional eight-step tick order
nodes.rationale: Advance restart/terminal phases, apply held actions and stamina, resolve pitch/player interactions, process guarded kicks, update attachment or free-ball motion, resolve pickup/steal, detect swept goal/boundary crossings, then emit events and publish state. Provisional: kick-and-boundary in one tick, simultaneous pickup and ownership-changing collisions need tests.

nodes.label: [Approved starting] x-right/y-down coordinates
nodes.rationale: Logical coordinates are x right, y down; facing is radians with zero east and positive clockwise. Physical forward is (cos, sin), while an observation may order features as (sin, cos) - a feature ordering, not a geometric vector. The original plan's y-up pitch drawing is superseded.

nodes.label: [Open] Effort-zero braking discontinuity
nodes.rationale: Tiny positive effort uses the active 320 units/s² acceleration limit and therefore brakes harder than effort exactly zero, which uses idle braking 40. The discontinuity is tested but should be revisited during movement/stamina tuning.

nodes.label: [Implemented] Free-ball constant-deceleration integration
nodes.rationale: Each tick preserves direction, subtracts deceleration*dt from speed without reversing, and integrates average speed over the moving portion, so partial-tick stopping is exact. This differs intentionally from the player's approximate velocity-first update. The ball is not pitch-clamped and emits no goal/out-of-bounds event; no tunnelling-safe detection is claimed.
nodes.source_location: ## Free ball: first A3 increment, lines 115-146

nodes.label: [Implemented] Engine module map
nodes.rationale: game/actions.py holds the typed nine-direction movement intent and effort; config.py immutable validated config; player.py snapshots/acceleration/braking/facing/bounds; stamina.py; ball.py; simulation.py reset/swap/stepping/clock/finish. python -m game is headless inspection. No kick, possession, goals, score, player collision, renderer, Gymnasium wrapper or PPO encoding.

nodes.label: [Implemented] Stamina-first semi-implicit player update
nodes.rationale: Stamina updates first, then fatigued limits are derived from base config. Target velocity = direction * effort * max_speed; velocity moves toward it by at most acceleration*dt without overshoot; idle/zero effort brakes. Position uses the new velocity (semi-implicit Euler). Facing turns on the shortest arc, idle preserves it, and 180 degrees ties counterclockwise.

nodes.label: [Implemented] Pitch clamp with tangential sliding
nodes.rationale: Player centre is clamped at least player-radius inside each boundary; only outward normal velocity is cancelled, retaining tangential sliding and inward motion. There is no wall bounce, and requested effort is still consumed against a wall.

nodes.label: [Documented] Plan y-up and x/y-action superseded
nodes.rationale: The original plan's continuous x/y movement action is superseded by nine-direction + continuous effort/power + binary kick, and its y-up pitch drawing is superseded by x-right/y-down. These older statements must remain labeled as historical, not current.

nodes.label: [Planned] Remaining Member A mechanics
nodes.rationale: Still to do: controlled attachment/owner/last toucher; facing kick with power and request expiry/cooldown; player-ball and player-player collisions, recovery, steal contest; swept goal/boundary checks, scores, restart placement; renderer/environment equivalence and throughput. Restarts currently only freeze state, the ball can leave the pitch without scoring, and A3 is incomplete.

nodes.label: [Documented] Source authority and history
nodes.rationale: The original Word plan supplies assignment context, AGENTS.md records newer student-approved decisions, docs/engine.md documents actual behavior/tests, and README/pyproject/uv.lock/.python-version describe setup. The graph must preserve historical differences rather than silently merging them.

nodes.label: [Documented] Deterministic tests do not prove tuning or integration
nodes.norm_label: [documented] deterministic tests do not prove tuning or integration
nodes.rationale: Deterministic unit tests do not demonstrate realistic tuning, successful training or completed integration, especially with the full-stack import test excluded. Actual command results must be consulted rather than inferred test success.

nodes.label: [Planned] Held-out-seed multi-match validation
nodes.rationale: Evaluate on held-out seeds and both attacking sides, ideally about 100 matches per comparison if feasible, reporting sample size and uncertainty. Outcomes and goal difference matter more than rising shaped reward; steals and loose-ball recoveries stay distinct.

nodes.label: [Planned] Root entry-point scaffolds
nodes.rationale: play.py, observe.py, train.py, test.py and evaluate.ipynb are scaffold files only; the README explicitly labels them planned and none is a working game, trainer or evaluation result.

nodes.label: [Implemented] uv locked setup
nodes.rationale: uv validated with 0.12.15; .venv is recreated from pyproject.toml and uv.lock and never committed. Engine-only runs must include --only-group engine on both sync and run, otherwise the full stack may be installed.

nodes.label: [Proposed] Determinism invariant for seeded replay
nodes.rationale: Identical seed, initial state and action sequence must yield identical state trajectories within floating-point tolerance on the same runtime. No randomness is used yet, so reset currently has no seed argument or RNG state.

nodes.label: [Documented] Mentor/pair-programmer workflow
nodes.rationale: The human is learning: the student owns decisions, implementation understanding, tests and explanations. The agent should teach concepts, propose one small testable step, avoid writing code until asked, and never invent results or completed features.

nodes.label: [Documented] Renderer-independent pure simulation API
nodes.rationale: No Pygame calls, event loops, sleeping, display objects, wall-clock timing or training-framework imports in game/. The rendering layer reads state; the RL wrapper and agents call the same simulation through a documented interface.

nodes.label: [Documented] Reward arithmetic outside the engine
nodes.rationale: Member A exposes trustworthy transition events with explicit previous/new owners and event causes; Member C computes reward. Keeping reward arithmetic out of the physics engine preserves the simulation/reward boundary.

nodes.label: [Documented] Test-first checklist
nodes.rationale: Before implementing a mechanic, write down inputs, expected outputs, invariants, boundary cases, one tiny manual example and one automated test. After implementation report only tests actually executed with command, outcome and limitations; prefer deterministic unit tests over visual intuition.

nodes.label: [Historical difference] Original figure y-up; approved engine y-down
nodes.norm_label: [historical difference] original figure y-up; approved engine y-down
nodes.rationale: Resolved by the newer student-approved convention, not an open decision. See docs/project_review.md: Source authority and history.

nodes.label: [Implemented] graphify-out review artifacts
nodes.rationale: graphify-out/ contains graph.html for the interactive map, GRAPH_TREE.html for a file-oriented tree, GRAPH_REPORT.md for the text summary and graph.json for queries. The graph covers code, tests, current docs and the original Word plan; current decisions supersede older plan proposals.
